propositions.text: The applicant seeks to set aside the adjudicator's decision excluding the LP-04 position from the bargaining unit under paragraph 59(1)(g) of the FPSLRA.
propositions.quote: The applicant seeks to set aside the decision of an adjudicator of the Federal Public Sector Labour Relations and Employment Board (the FPSLREB) in Treasury Board (Department of Justice) v. Association of Justice Counsel, 2020 FPSLREB 59.

propositions.text: The adjudicator determined the LP-04 position should be excluded from the bargaining unit under paragraph 59(1)(g) of the FPSLRA.
propositions.quote: In that decision, the adjudicator determined that the LP-04 position in the Centre for Information Law and Privacy (CILP) within the Department of Justice should be excluded from the bargaining unit under paragraph 59(1)(g) of the Federal Public Sector Labour Relations Act

paragraphs.summary: The applicant seeks to set aside the adjudicator's decision excluding the LP-04 position from the bargaining unit under paragraph 59(1)(g) of the FPSLRA, the adjudicator's finding.

propositions.text: The adjudicator found the incumbent provided advice on Privacy Act and Access to Information Act in labour relations-sensitive matters.
propositions.quote: the adjudicator determined that the incumbent of the position in question was sometimes called upon to provide advice on issues under the Privacy Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. P-21 and the Access to Information Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. A-1 in the context of labour relations-sensitive matters.

propositions.text: The adjudicator concluded a sufficient intersection of labour relations, staffing and classification justified exclusion under paragraph 59(1)(g).
propositions.quote: there was accordingly a “sufficient intersection of labour relations, staffing and classification matters” to justify the exclusion due to the potential for a conflict of interest under paragraph 59(1)(g) of the FPSLRA.

propositions.text: The adjudicator found exclusion under paragraph 59(1)(c) was not warranted as the occupant did not provide advice on labour relations, staffing or classification issues themselves.
propositions.quote: The adjudicator, however, determined that an exclusion under paragraph 59(1)(c) of the FPSLRA was not warranted as the occupant of the position did not provide advice on labour relations, staffing or classification issues, themselves.

paragraphs.summary: The adjudicator found the incumbent provided advice on privacy and access issues in labour relations-sensitive matters, justifying exclusion under paragraph 59(1)(g), but not under 59(1)(c).

propositions.text: Paragraphs 59(1)(c), (g), and (h) of the FPSLRA define grounds for excluding positions from bargaining units.
propositions.quote: The relevant provisions in the FPSLRA provide: Application Demande 59 (1) ... (c) the occupant of the position provides advice on labour relations, staffing or classification; ... (g) the occupant of the position has duties and responsibilities not otherwise described ... for reasons of conflict of interest ...; or ... (h) the occupant of the position has ... duties and responsibilities confidential to the occupant of a position described in paragraph (b), (c), (d) or (f).

paragraphs.summary: Paragraphs 59(1)(c), (g), and (h) of the FPSLRA define grounds for excluding positions from bargaining units.

propositions.text: The applicant asserts the adjudicator's decision was unreasonable for two principal reasons.
propositions.quote: Before us, the applicant asserts that the decision of the adjudicator was unreasonable, principally for two reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant asserts the adjudicator's decision was unreasonable for two principal reasons.

propositions.text: The adjudicator unreasonably interpreted the FPSLRA provisions, which should be read narrowly to protect constitutional rights.
propositions.quote: the adjudicator unreasonably interpreted the relevant statutory provisions, which should be read narrowly as they limit the constitutionally-protected right to join and be represented by a trade union.

propositions.text: Parliament intended labour relations exclusions to fall under paragraphs 59(1)(c) or (h), not (g).
propositions.quote: Parliament contemplated that all labour relations-related exclusions would fall under either paragraph 59(1)(c) or (h) of the FPSLRA and that it was therefore not reasonable to interpret paragraph 59(1)(g) of the Act as including duties in relations to labour relations matters that do not rise to the level of being covered by either paragraph 59(1)(c) or (h) of the FPSLRA.

propositions.text: Interpreting paragraph 59(1)(g) broadly impermissibly broadens labour relations exclusions.
propositions.quote: such interpretation impermissibly broadens the scope of the labour relations exclusions in the FPSLRA.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant argues the adjudicator unreasonably interpreted the FPSLRA, wrongly broadening labour relations exclusions under paragraph 59(1)(g).

propositions.text: The adjudicator unreasonably relied on the incumbent's seniority and experience, which is irrelevant to the inquiry.
propositions.quote: the adjudicator unreasonably premised his decision in large part on the fact that the incumbent in the LP-04 position within the CILP was a senior, experienced lawyer.

propositions.text: Case law requires examining duties of the position, not attributes of the incumbent.
propositions.quote: case law of the FPSLREB requires examination of the duties required of the position as opposed to the attributes of the incumbent.

propositions.text: If seniority mattered, no senior government lawyer could be unionized, contrary to Parliament's intent.
propositions.quote: were it otherwise, no senior government lawyer could ever be unionized, which was clearly not the intent of Parliament when it extended collective bargaining rights to lawyers working for the federal government in 2005.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant argues the adjudicator wrongly relied on the incumbent's seniority, contrary to case law and Parliament's intent.

propositions.text: I disagree with both of the applicant's submissions.
propositions.quote: With respect, I disagree with both submissions.

paragraphs.summary: The court disagrees with both of the applicant's submissions.

propositions.text: The applicant cited no authority that paragraph 59(1)(g) cannot apply to conflicts from advice like that given by the incumbent.
propositions.quote: the applicant has cited no authority in support of his contention that paragraph 59(1)(g) of the FPSLRA cannot apply to conflicts or potential conflicts arising from the provision of advice of precisely the sort given by the incumbent in the LP-04 position in this case.

propositions.text: This case is similar to earlier FPSLREB decisions excluding incumbents providing advice with potential impacts like here.
propositions.quote: this case is similar to earlier decisions of the FPSLREB ... where incumbents were excluded because they provided advice on topics that had potential impacts akin to those in the present case

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no authority against applying paragraph 59(1)(g) here and notes similar earlier FPSLREB decisions.

propositions.text: Paragraph 59(1)(g) of the FPSLRA grants broad discretion to exclude employees based on duties and responsibilities.
propositions.quote: the provision “[…] confers on the PSLRB a very broad discretion to exclude an employee on the basis of aspects of his or her duties and responsibilities […].”

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 59(1)(g) grants broad discretion to exclude employees based on duties and responsibilities.

propositions.text: The adjudicator's interpretation of paragraph 59(1)(g) was reasonable.
propositions.quote: The adjudicator’s interpretation of paragraph 59(1)(g) of the FPSLRA was therefore reasonable.

paragraphs.summary: The adjudicator's interpretation of paragraph 59(1)(g) was reasonable, the court finds.

propositions.text: The adjudicator did not base his decision largely on the incumbent's seniority and experience.
propositions.quote: I disagree that he premised the decision in large part on the fact that the incumbent in the LP-04 position was a senior, experienced lawyer.

propositions.text: The adjudicator's comments about seniority were contextually responsive to suggestions about excluding junior lawyers.
propositions.quote: The comments made by the adjudicator ... must be read in context and are responsive to suggestions that the employer could have ensured all labour relations-sensitive discussions were held with the more junior excluded lawyer in the CILP.

propositions.text: The adjudicator explained why excluding a senior position was permissible.
propositions.quote: the adjudicator merely explained why it was permissible for the employer to also exclude a senior position within the CILP.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the adjudicator did not improperly rely on seniority but explained why excluding a senior position was permissible.

propositions.text: The adjudicator highlighted duties causing conflict, such as advice on privacy and access issues in litigation with bargaining agents.
propositions.quote: the adjudicator highlights the duties assigned to the LP-04 position that gave rise to a conflict of interest, such as providing advice in respect of privacy or access to information issues in connection with litigation between the employer and the bargaining agents.

propositions.text: There was evidence that the incumbent performed these duties before and after reorganization, even without managing subordinates.
propositions.quote: there was evidence before the adjudicator that indicated that such duties had been performed by the incumbent both before and after the reorganization in the CILP, when the incumbent was no longer charged with managing subordinates

paragraphs.summary: The adjudicator highlighted duties causing conflict; the respondent notes evidence the incumbent performed these duties before and after reorganization.

propositions.text: The adjudicator did not unreasonably base his decision on the incumbent's experience.
propositions.quote: The adjudicator therefore did not unreasonably base his decision on the fact that the incumbent in the LP-04 position within the CILP possessed significant experience.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the adjudicator did not unreasonably base his decision on the incumbent's experience.

propositions.text: The application is dismissed with costs fixed at $2,500.
propositions.quote: I would accordingly dismiss this application, with costs, fixed in the agreed-upon all-inclusive amount of $2,500.00, which I believe to be reasonable.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the application with costs fixed at $2,500.
